title: A Study in Healthy Participants With Elevated LDL-C to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics of CS060380
official: A Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled, Sequential, Multiple Ascending Dose (MAD) Study Following Oral Administration in Healthy Participants With Elevated LDL-C to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics of CS060380
summary: A study in Healthy Participants with Elevated LDL-C to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics of CS060380.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. The participant provided signed and dated informed consent.
2. Male or female aged 18-65 years (inclusive).
3. Fasting LDL-C \>110 mg/dL (2.85 mmol/L) at screening.
4. Female participants must meet one of the following:

   1. Postmenopausal status confirmed by follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) testing, or
   2. Surgically sterile (medically documented), or
   3. If with childbearing potential, the participant must agree to use at least one highly effective contraceptive method in combination with an additional effective contraceptive method from study initiation until 3 months after the last dose, or
   4. Complete abstinence (if agreed by the participant).

   Male participants, even if surgically sterilized (e.g., vasectomy), must:
   1. Use effective barrier contraception and refrain from sperm donation throughout the study and for 3 months after the last dose, or
   2. Complete abstinence (if agreed upon by the participant). Refer to Section 9.4 for detailed contraceptive requirements.
5. Normal renal function (estimated glomerular filtration rate \[eGFR\] ≥ 80 mL/min/1.73 m², calculated using the CKD-EPI equation).
6. Good general health, as judged by the Investigator based on: medical/surgical history, complete physical examination, vital signs, laboratory tests, and 12-lead ECG results (all findings either normal or with no clinically significant abnormalities).
7. No significant medical history; assessed to be in good general health at screening, with evaluations completed ≤ 28 days before the first dose.
8. Willingness and ability to: Understand and comply with study procedures/restrictions, complete the trial as planned and communicate effectively with the Investigator.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Individuals with special dietary requirements unable to comply with standardized diets.
2. Females who are pregnant or lactating, those with pregnancy plans within 3 months post-trial, or female participants with positive pregnancy tests during screening/baseline periods.
3. Participants with febrile illness or active infection within 7 days prior to the first dose of the investigational drug.
4. Participants with positive urine drug screening results.
5. Participants with a history of drug/substance abuse within 5 years prior to the trial or positive drug screening at Day -1.
6. Participants receiving lipid-lowering therapy or with LDL-C \> 190 mg/dL, or those with a history of coronary artery disease, cardiac arrhythmias, unexplained syncope, or family history of sudden cardiac arrest.
7. Participants with a history of QTc prolongation:

   1. QTcF ≥ 450 ms during screening;
   2. Hypocalcemia or family history of long QT syndrome;
   3. Use of QT/QTc-prolonging medications;
   4. ECG abnormalities deemed clinically significant by the Investigator.
8. Tobacco or nicotine product use within 3 months prior to screening or during the study until discharge.
9. Use of other investigational drugs within 40 days prior to enrollment or within ≥ 5 half-lives (whichever is longer).
10. Positive infectious disease screening results during screening (HIV antibody, HBsAg, HCV antibody).
11. Clinically significant laboratory abnormalities per Investigator judgment during screening.
12. Presence of clinically significant hypertension, defined as systolic blood pressure (SBP) \> 145 mmHg and/or diastolic blood pressure (DBP) \> 90 mmHg, at Screening or Admission.
13. Blood loss \> 50 mL within 40 days or \> 500 mL within 56 days prior to dosing.
14. Regular alcohol consumption (\> 1 unit/day) within 1 month prior to screening or positive alcohol test at screening or admission. \[1 unit = 150 mL wine, 360 mL beer, or 45 mL 40% alcohol\]. Alcohol consumption within 48 hours predose or during CRU stays.
15. Prescription/OTC medication use within 14 days prior to admission (Day -1) or ≥ 5 half-lives (whichever is longer); or use of any of the inhibitors or induces as listed in Appendix 1, CYP3A-, p-glycoprotein- (p-gp) or breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP)-modulating substances (e.g., herbs, grapefruit) within 14 days predose or ≥ 5 half-lives.
16. Thyroid disease history or clinically significant thyroid test abnormalities.
17. Hypersensitivity to thyroid medications.
18. Conditions potentially affecting drug ADME (e.g., gastrectomy, cholecystectomy, inflammatory bowel disease).
19. Clinically significant comorbidities (e.g., GI, renal, hepatic, neurological, hematological, endocrine, oncological, pulmonary, immunological, psychiatric, or cardiovascular diseases) that may compromise study conduct/interpretation or pose risks per Investigator assessment.
20. Hypersensitivity to investigational drug components, specific allergy history (asthma, urticaria, eczema), or atopic predisposition (allergy to ≥ 2 drugs/foods like milk/pollen).
21. Any condition deemed by the Investigator to jeopardize participant safety or study integrity.
22. Abnormal thyroid function tests (total/free T3, total/free T4, TSH) beyond reference ranges during screening.
23. Troponin \> ULN during screening or Day -1 periods.
24. Presence of any psychiatric disorder or impaired mental capacity that may compromise the ability to provide informed consent, affect the assessment of efficacy, or impair compliance with the study protocol.
25. Any other condition that, in the opinion of the investigator, may jeopardize the safety of the subject or compromise the quality of the clinical study.
